title: peatmoor ivyhurst sud exchange segmentation plan
instruction:
You are the medical operations manager at Peatmoor Analytics, which manages Ivyhurst Studios’ co-located primary-care practice and licensed substance-use-disorder service. Estelle Calderon needs an approval-ready operating plan for joining the regional health information exchange in October without exposing records the service treats as specially protected. Both services use one EHR and one patient chart. The platform can segregate outbound data only at the encounter level; it cannot selectively remove individual problems or medications, and clinicians rely on the unified internal medication list. Splitting the chart would disrupt that clinical view, walling off the whole practice would undermine the exchange commitment, and a consent-heavy model would exceed the team’s capacity for recurring manual review. The practice is also mid-change: over the next eight weeks, the SUD service is moving from shared scheduling templates to dedicated departments and encounter types, while historical and already-booked encounters will retain inconsistent labels. The plan therefore has to work during that transition as well as after the new structure is established. There is also a rare but high-consequence case to cover: another treating facility may urgently request relevant SUD information for an unconscious patient when delay could create serious harm and ordinary consent cannot be obtained. Prepare one recommended segmentation configuration, explain the material privacy and operational boundaries, identify the changes authorized from the current configuration, and set aside the credible alternatives. Include the assumptions behind your projection of transition-period and end-state outcomes, but do not invent patient volumes, staffing levels, costs, system capabilities, or legal conclusions that the facts do not support. This is for an executive decision, not a legal brief or an EHR click-through guide, and it must be usable by the implementation and compliance leads after approval. Keep it to four pages maximum. Write the final document into the top level of the working directory using exactly the filename `exchange_segmentation_operating_plan.docx`.

---

Write your finished work to the **top level of the current working directory**, using exactly these filenames:

- `exchange_segmentation_operating_plan.docx` — Executive operating plan recommending a data-segmentation configuration, defining transition and end-state operation, and documenting rejected alternatives. (Must be written to the top level of the working directory using the exact filename exchange_segmentation_operating_plan.docx.; Must not exceed four rendered pages.; Must present one recommended configuration and identify the authorized changes from the current configuration.; Must address both the eight-week transition and the end state.; Must address the rare urgent request involving an unconscious patient.; Must not invent unsupported patient volumes, staffing levels, costs, system capabilities, or definitive legal conclusions.; Must not be an EHR click-through guide.)

Nothing outside those filenames is collected. A correct file written anywhere else, or under any other name, scores zero.

gold.note: DOCX 正文与表格单元格文字提取；不还原分页、字体与版式。
gold.text:
HIE exchange segmentation operating plan
Ivyhurst Studios  |  Decision requested: approve October configuration subject to gates below  |  Owner: Medical Operations Manager
RECOMMEND
Keep one internal chart. Use encounter-based outbound routing: eligible primary-care encounters may transmit; protected SUD encounters, mixed encounters, and unresolved encounters do not transmit routinely. Suppress outbound longitudinal medication and problem-list payloads until protected provenance can be reliably controlled.
1. Approval requested and decision boundaries
Authorize the configuration and governance changes in Section 3 for an October launch only after Compliance validates applicability and disclosure rules for the SUD program records, the HIE validates the supported feed controls, and the acceptance tests in Section 6 pass. This is an operating decision, not a legal conclusion. Qualifying SUD program records may carry heightened confidentiality protections based on program status and record provenance; licensure alone, addiction-related content alone, or placement in the shared EHR does not settle that question. A shared chart does not extinguish protections that attach to protected records.
The exchange commitment is a contractual and care-coordination objective, not independent disclosure authority. Likewise, an HIE participation agreement, notice of privacy practices, routine treatment consent, minimum-necessary review, or a technical break-glass tool does not by itself authorize disclosure of protected SUD information. Once authority exists, minimum-necessary and role controls further limit release. Recipient obligations, exchange controls, and audit trails reduce downstream risk; they cannot make improper use or redisclosure technically impossible.
2. Recommended configuration: outbound by encounter; internal chart remains unified
Content / condition
Routine HIE rule
Operating boundary
Eligible primary-care encounter
Transmit under ordinary privacy and exchange controls, unless its content or linked artifacts would reveal protected SUD treatment.
A patient’s use of the SUD service alone does not suppress otherwise eligible primary-care care.
Protected SUD encounter
Exclude by default from routine HIE release.
Release only through a validated, documented patient authorization or a narrow applicable exception.
Mixed or unresolved encounter
Hold from outbound transmission; mark restricted pending classification review/correction.
No clinician “best judgment” auto-release. A cleared, corrected encounter may be released prospectively only when authority and content are confirmed.
Longitudinal medication + problem payloads
Do not send chart-level medication-list or problem-list payloads in this configuration.
The EHR cannot segment individual problem-list or medication-list entries for exchange. Internal clinicians retain the unified medication list.
Linked artifacts and metadata
Inherit/reconcile the parent encounter restriction for orders, results, referrals, documents, notes, attachments, and routing artifacts.
Suppress revealing encounter/department names, service labels and alerts from outbound data; use neutral routing labels where needed. Identity/demographics may support matching, not disclosure of SUD participation.

3. Changes authorized from the current configuration
Approve now
Preserve / do not change
Enable encounter-level outbound routing; create a default restricted class for protected, mixed, and unresolved encounters; disable longitudinal medication and problem-list feeds; map linked artifacts and metadata to parent sensitivity; add exception queue, audit fields, role permissions, incident containment and correction workflow.
One EHR, one patient chart, and the unified internal medication list. No patient-level wall-off, chart split, problem-level filtering, medication-level filtering, or recurring manual review of every exchange transaction.
Complete the eight-week move to dedicated SUD departments and encounter types; configure them as the primary end-state routing signal. Maintain an exception path for mixed content, misclassification, and uncertain scope—labels improve reliability but do not conclusively determine legal coverage.
Existing historical and already-booked encounter labels are not treated as reliable release authority during transition.

4. Operating model: transition, end state, and exceptions
Period / pathway
Rule and accountable action
Expected qualitative outcome / assumption
Eight-week transition
For historical and already-booked encounters, validate against provenance/content mapping before release; do not use inconsistent labels as the sole basis. Unresolved before transmission remains restricted, is routed to the designated classification reviewer, and is not released until disposition. Corrected sensitivity/department classifications are approved by the classification lead; stop queued release, assess any prior transmission, preserve audit evidence, and invoke incident response when warranted.
Assumptions: labels are unreliable during staged conversion and recurring manual capacity is constrained. More holds and targeted validations are expected; routine eligible encounters continue where reliably classified.
End state
Dedicated SUD department plus encounter types route protected encounters to default exclusion. Primary-care routing remains open only when the encounter and linked artifacts pass the protected-content screen. Mixed/misclassified content follows the same restricted exception path.
More consistent routing is expected as the dedicated structure stabilizes. Residual risk remains from mixed content, incorrect assignment, and non-segmentable longitudinal data; these feeds stay suppressed.
Patient-authorized release (exception)
Release manager verifies a valid, documented authorization for the intended recipient, specific information, purpose, and duration; then releases only the authorized scope. Revalidate before each later release; stop on expiration, revocation, or material change.
Exception only—not baseline architecture—so manual work is limited to requested releases rather than every HIE event.
Urgent unconscious-patient request
Authorized clinical/privacy decision maker may use a narrow medical-emergency pathway only when relevant information is needed immediately for treatment and delay risks serious harm, ordinary permission cannot be obtained, and Compliance’s validated rule permits it. Disclose only relevant emergency information; do not automatically open the full SUD record. Technical break-glass enables access, not disclosure authority.
Promptly record emergency basis, requester/recipient, information disclosed, date/time, and authorizing actor; conduct follow-up review.

5. Alternatives set aside
Alternative
Why not the baseline (same decision tests: privacy, clinical continuity, HIE participation, capacity, technology)
Split charts
Rejected: fragments the unified medication view and introduces reconciliation and duplicate-record risk; it is disproportionate when encounter-based external controls can preserve the internal chart.
Suppress the whole practice
Rejected: over-restricts eligible primary-care exchange, undermining the participation commitment and care-coordination objective without adding a targeted safeguard.
Broad recurring consent management
Rejected: requires ongoing manual review at a level the team cannot sustain and adds expiration/revocation and routing failure points. Authorization remains available for controlled exceptions.

6. Implementation, assurance, and go-live gates
Function
Accountability and acceptance evidence
Classification & clinical validation
Clinical operations owns encounter taxonomy, mixed-content escalation, correction authority, and clinical validation. Privacy/Compliance validates scope assumptions and escalates genuinely uncertain coverage or disclosure authority; routine eligible routing does not require legal review.
Exchange configuration & privacy approval
HIE/IT configures encounter routing, linked-artifact/metadata controls, longitudinal-feed suppression, role separation, and outbound audit capture. Privacy approves exception and emergency workflow. Only designated roles may classify, override, or release protected encounters; ordinary exchange users cannot.
Pre-go-live tests
Demonstrate both permitted and prohibited transmissions: eligible primary care; protected SUD; mixed; unreliable historical labels; medication and problem lists; linked orders/results/referrals/documents/attachments; consent exception lifecycle; and medical emergency documentation. Confirm demographics match without service-affiliation leakage.
Audit, monitoring & containment
For every routine and exception release, retain rule/authority, actor, recipient, time, and data released. Review misclassification, unauthorized release, failed authorized release, and manual-exception workload. A failed segmentation test or suspected improper transmission triggers authority to suspend affected outbound routes, preserve evidence, investigate/notify under applicable process, remediate, retest, and resume only with approval.

Decision record
Approve the recommended encounter-based configuration subject to the stated compliance validation, negative-disclosure testing, and containment authority. This choice preserves clinical continuity internally, enables eligible primary-care participation externally, and fails safely where classification or authority is uncertain.

spec.professional_context: Peatmoor Analytics is preparing Ivyhurst Studios’ integrated primary-care and SUD service for participation in a health information exchange. The operating plan will support an executive configuration decision with significant privacy, clinical-safety, contractual, and implementation consequences.
difficulty_sources: Choosing one workable configuration despite competing privacy, clinical-continuity, exchange-participation, and staffing constraints
Applying heightened SUD confidentiality principles without enough facts to make an unconditional legal coverage determination
Designing around encounter-only segmentation and non-segmentable longitudinal medication and problem data
Creating controls that differ appropriately between an unstable transition period and the end state
Separating a rare medical-emergency pathway from routine disclosure guidance
Producing defensible qualitative outcome projections without inventing operational figures

authoring_plan.solver_instance: A medical and health services manager with responsibility for privacy-sensitive exchange operations must create an executive-ready operating plan from occupational knowledge, without source files or live research.
authoring_plan.behaviour_specification: The solution should make one conservative but workable call: retain the unified internal chart; allow eligible primary-care encounters to flow; suppress protected SUD encounters from routine exchange; control non-segmentable longitudinal medication and problem payloads so they cannot bypass encounter segmentation; use narrowly governed patient-authorized and medical-emergency release pathways; and treat uncertain or mixed records as restricted until resolved.
authoring_plan.intended_verdict: Approve the encounter-based configuration subject to documented compliance applicability validation, negative disclosure testing, and controlled transition safeguards. Reject chart splitting, whole-practice suppression, and broad recurring consent management as baseline designs.
imperfections_and_tensions: Primary care and the licensed SUD service share one EHR and one chart.
The EHR can segregate outbound data only by encounter, not by individual problem or medication entry.
The unified internal medication list is clinically important and must not be destroyed to solve the exchange problem.
The SUD service is moving from shared scheduling templates to dedicated departments and encounter types over eight weeks.
Historical and already-booked encounters have inconsistent labels, so automatic release based solely on current labels would be unsafe during transition.
Manual consent operations can support exceptions but cannot sustainably govern every exchange event.
The medical-emergency case is rare but must be separately governed because routine guidance is insufficient and misuse could cause severe privacy harm.
Licensure and addiction-related content do not, by themselves, provide enough facts for a categorical legal coverage conclusion.
gold_relationships: Routine release eligibility must depend on encounter provenance, classification reliability, applicable disclosure authority, and the absence of linked protected content.
Protected SUD encounters are withheld by default; valid patient permission or a narrow applicable exception may authorize a controlled release.
Eligible primary-care encounters remain exchangeable unless their content or linked artifacts would reveal protected SUD treatment.
Mixed encounters and unresolved classifications fail closed until reviewed or corrected.

During transition, historical or inconsistent labels require validation, mapping, or a release hold; after transition, dedicated department and encounter types become the primary routing control but not an absolute legal conclusion.

Outbound chart-level medication and problem payloads must not be allowed to expose entries whose protected provenance cannot be separated. Internal clinician access to the unified list remains intact.
Orders, results, referrals, notes, attachments, and revealing metadata inherit or are reconciled with the protection of the originating encounter.
Patient permission is scoped, documented, time-bound as applicable, and subject to lifecycle controls; it is an exception workflow rather than the baseline architecture.

The medical-emergency pathway requires a treatment-linked serious-harm threshold, disclosure limited to relevant information, authorized action, and documentation of who, what, why, when, and to whom.
A technical break-glass capability permits access but does not itself establish disclosure authority.

The split-chart option fails the clinical-continuity test; whole-practice suppression fails the proportionality and exchange-participation test; broad recurring consent management fails the staffing and reliability test.

Transition projections should anticipate more holds and manual validation because labels are unreliable. End-state projections should anticipate more consistent routing but retain residual risks from mixed content and non-segmentable longitudinal data.
Go-live approval depends on positive and negative transmission tests, including linked artifacts and longitudinal feeds, with containment authority for failures.
The authorized change description must identify the new encounter-routing, feed-suppression, exception, audit, and governance controls while preserving the internal unified chart.

doctrinal_rule_and_nonclaim_pairs.rule: Heightened confidentiality may attach to qualifying SUD program records and follow the record into a shared system.
doctrinal_rule_and_nonclaim_pairs.must_not_claim: Every addiction-related fact or every record created by a licensed service automatically has identical status without an applicability analysis.

doctrinal_rule_and_nonclaim_pairs.rule: Exchange disclosure requires applicable authority and compliance with governing confidentiality controls.
doctrinal_rule_and_nonclaim_pairs.must_not_claim: The exchange contract, routine treatment consent, or technical connectivity independently authorizes all disclosures.

doctrinal_rule_and_nonclaim_pairs.rule: Minimum-necessary and role-based controls remain relevant after disclosure authority is established.
doctrinal_rule_and_nonclaim_pairs.must_not_claim: Applying minimum-necessary review creates authority that otherwise does not exist.

doctrinal_rule_and_nonclaim_pairs.rule: Patient-authorized disclosure must be governed according to its valid scope and lifecycle.
doctrinal_rule_and_nonclaim_pairs.must_not_claim: One blanket or indefinite consent automatically covers every recipient, purpose, and future disclosure.

doctrinal_rule_and_nonclaim_pairs.rule: A narrow medical-emergency pathway may be available when its substantive conditions are met.
doctrinal_rule_and_nonclaim_pairs.must_not_claim: Any urgent request, unconscious patient, or use of break-glass automatically permits release of the complete record.

doctrinal_rule_and_nonclaim_pairs.rule: Recipient obligations, exchange controls, and audit evidence can reduce downstream risk.
doctrinal_rule_and_nonclaim_pairs.must_not_claim: Segmentation or exchange participation makes unauthorized downstream use technically impossible.

doctrinal_rule_and_nonclaim_pairs.rule: Dedicated departments and encounter types improve classification and routing reliability.
doctrinal_rule_and_nonclaim_pairs.must_not_claim: A department label conclusively determines legal coverage or eliminates mixed-content risk.

authoring_plan.reachability_check: All rubric requirements are assessable from the single DOCX and derive from the stated operational facts or standard healthcare privacy, records-management, clinical-safety, and HIE implementation practice. No item depends on a hidden local code, vendor-specific screen, external source, exact case count, or undisclosed numeric answer. A four-page document can satisfy the rubric through a concise recommendation, configuration rules, transition and exception controls, alternatives comparison, implementation controls, and assumptions.

deliverables.description: Executive operating plan recommending a data-segmentation configuration, defining transition and end-state operation, and documenting rejected alternatives.
constraints: Must be written to the top level of the working directory using the exact filename exchange_segmentation_operating_plan.docx.
Must not exceed four rendered pages.
Must present one recommended configuration and identify the authorized changes from the current configuration.
Must address both the eight-week transition and the end state.
Must address the rare urgent request involving an unconscious patient.
Must not invent unsupported patient volumes, staffing levels, costs, system capabilities, or definitive legal conclusions.
Must not be an EHR click-through guide.
